title: Cartesian tensor pullback preserves flat finite presentation and proper support
statement: Let $X_i,X_j,S_i,S_j$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f_i:X_i\to S_i$ and $f_j:X_j\to S_j$ locally of finite type [def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $p:X_j\to X_i$ and $k:S_j\to S_i$ give a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change], so $X_j\cong X_i\times_{S_i}S_j$. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal O_{X_i}$-module [pqf-def-coherent], flat over $S_i$ (its sections on every affine open mapping into an affine base open are flat over the base ring), with support proper over $S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Then $p^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is finitely presented, flat over $S_j$ in the same affine-local sense, and has support proper over $S_j$.

proof.text: Compare tensorPullback p and the native Scheme.Modules.pullback p by uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward p. Apply the proved source instance Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.FiniteDescent) and transport finite presentation across the comparison isomorphism. No separate finite-presentation theorem is introduced.

Apply relativelyFlat_module_pullback fi k M hflat on the canonical fibre product. Let a be hcart.isoPullback.hom. Its composites with the canonical projections are p and fj. Tensor-pullback composition and the comparison with native pullback, followed by restrictFunctorIsoPullback for the isomorphism a, identify p* M with the restriction along a of the canonical pullback. The private flatOver_restrict lemma is proved directly: each affine test open maps to an affine open under the open immersion a; apply old relative flatness there, and use comp_appLE and appLE_appIso_inv to identify the scalar action. The private flatOver_of_iso lemma transports affine-section flatness through the evaluation isomorphism restricted to the base ring. These elementary glue proofs give the required IsFlatOver fj without a new hole.

Choose the closed support Z from hproper, and construct Zj as its closed inverse image under p. Finite presentation supplies quasi-coherence and finite type; finiteType_module_support_pullback identifies Zj with the pulled-back support. The existential structure equivalence of closed_subset_proper_over_base_properties supplies a closed immersion i:T→Xi with range Z and proper composite i followed by fi. Pull it back along p; its second projection j is a closed immersion with range p inverse-image Z by Scheme.Pullback.range_snd. Paste its pullback square vertically with hcart: the composite j followed by fj is the base change of the proper map i followed by fi, hence proper by MorphismProperty.of_isPullback. Apply the same closed-subset structure equivalence to Zj and this closed immersion. This gives proper support without constructing a module on the closed subscheme.

lean.statement:
theorem tensorPullback_flat_proper_support
    {Xi Xj Si Sj : Scheme.{u}}
    (fi : Xi ⟶ Si) (fj : Xj ⟶ Sj) [LocallyOfFiniteType fi] [LocallyOfFiniteType fj]
    (p : Xj ⟶ Xi) (k : Sj ⟶ Si) (hcart : IsPullback p fj fi k)
    (M : Xi.Modules) [M.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hflat : M.IsFlatOver fi) (hproper : Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver fi M) :
    (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj p M).IsFinitePresentation ∧
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj p M).IsFlatOver fj ∧
      Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver fj (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj p M)
